Candy Corn Dip

Instaread

Candy Corn Dip is a fun, no-bake Halloween treat with colorful orange and white swirls that come together in about 10 minutes. At just $0.69 per serving, it’s an affordable dessert for Halloween parties, classroom treats, or family gatherings.

Want to save this recipe?

I love putting this out when we have people over for Halloween because the bright colors make it stand out on the dessert table. It’s especially fun to serve with cookies, graham crackers, or fruit for dipping.

Don’t worry if you’re not a fan of the actual candy. This dip doesn’t taste like candy corn. It’s a smooth, creamy white chocolate dip that’s just inspired by the colors. It’s an affordable dessert for Halloween parties, classroom treats, or family gatherings.

Why You’ll Love This Recipe!

  • Ready in About 10 Minutes: This quick dessert comes together fast, making it easy to prepare when you need a last-minute Halloween treat.
  • No-Bake and Kid-Friendly: There’s no oven or candy thermometer needed, and kids can help with simple steps like stirring and creating the colorful swirls.
  • Budget-Friendly: Affordable ingredients like pudding mix, whipped topping, and food coloring make this a fun treat without a big grocery bill.
  • Great for Sharing: The festive colors make it a fun choice for Halloween parties, potlucks, classroom celebrations, or family get-togethers.

With more than 14 years of baking and creating recipes, I’ve learned that the recipes people trust most are the ones that are easy to make and easy to share. I’ve spent years testing desserts in my own kitchen, and this is one I’d happily make for a Halloween celebration.

You may also want to make Candy Corn Cookies and Candy Popcorn.

Ingredients

  • White Chocolate Instant Pudding Mix: Creates the creamy base and adds a smooth white chocolate flavor. Use instant pudding mix so it thickens properly without cooking. You can also try using Vanilla or Cheesecake-flavored instant pudding mix if that’s what you have on hand.
  • Cold Milk: Whisked with the pudding mix to create a thick, creamy consistency. Keep the milk cold to help the pudding set properly.
  • Cream Cheese: Adds richness and a slight tang that balances the sweetness of the pudding and powdered sugar. Soften it to room temperature for the smoothest dip.
  • Powdered Sugar: Adds sweetness and blends easily into the cream cheese without leaving a gritty texture.
  • Vanilla Extract: Enhances the white chocolate flavor and adds a warm, classic flavor to the creamy mixture.
  • Whipped Topping: Lightens the cream cheese and pudding mixture while giving the dip its fluffy, scoopable texture. Thaw it completely before mixing.
  • Orange Gel Food Coloring: Creates the bright orange color needed for the candy corn-inspired design. Gel coloring provides strong color without adding extra liquid to the dip.
  • Candy Corn: Adds a festive finishing touch and makes the candy corn theme instantly recognizable. Arrange a few pieces on top just before serving.
  • Orange, Yellow, and White Sprinkles: Add extra color and texture while helping create the classic candy corn look. Use them as a topping or sprinkle them around the candy corn garnish.

Step By Step Instructions

Step 1. Beat the cream cheese until smooth.

Step 2. Add the powdered sugar and vanilla extract and beat until combined.

Step 3. In a separate bowl, whisk the pudding mix and cold milk for about 2 minutes, until thickened. It’s normal if it still looks slightly thin right after whisking. Instant pudding keeps setting for a few minutes, so let it sit briefly before moving on if it needs it.

Step 4. Fold the pudding mixture into the cream cheese mixture until smooth.

Step 5. Gently fold in the whipped topping until combined.

Step 6. Reserve about ¼ cup of the mixture and set aside. Add orange gel food coloring to the remaining mixture until your desired color is reached.

Step 7. Spread the orange dip into a serving bowl. Dollop the reserved white mixture on top and gently swirl with a toothpick to create a candy corn-inspired design.

Step 8. Garnish with candy corn and sprinkles. Chill for 30 minutes before serving.

Pro Tips

  • Add candy corn just before serving: The candy can soften if it sits in the dip too long, so add it as a garnish right before serving.
  • Don’t overmix: Mix the ingredients just until combined and smooth. Overmixing after adding the whipped topping can make the dip less light and fluffy.
  • Use gel food coloring: Gel coloring gives you a bright orange color without adding extra liquid to the dip. Add a little at a time until you reach the shade you want.
  • Chill before serving: Refrigerate the dip before serving to help it firm up and allow the flavors to come together.
  • Add sprinkles last: Add the orange, yellow, and white sprinkles shortly before serving so they maintain their color and texture.
  • Serve with dippers: Pair the dip with vanilla wafers, graham crackers, pretzels, shortbread cookies, or fresh fruit.
  • Keep it chilled: Since the dip contains cream cheese and whipped topping, keep it refrigerated until you’re ready to serve.
  • Make it ahead: Prepare the dip earlier in the day and add the candy corn and sprinkles shortly before serving for the best presentation.

What to Serve With Candy Corn Dip

Vanilla wafers, graham crackers, pretzels, shortbread cookies, and apple slices are the classic choices, but a few more ideas can round out your dessert table:

  • Pretzel rods for a salty-sweet combination
  • Rice Krispie treats, cut into small squares
  • Pumpkin spice or cinnamon graham crackers for a seasonal twist
  • Fresh fruit skewers — strawberries, banana slices, or apple wedges threaded onto skewers make it easy for guests to grab and dip without crowding the bowl

Bringing This to a Classroom Party?

Skip the shared bowl and portion the dip into small individual cups instead. It’s easier to hand out, avoids any double-dipping concerns, and makes cleanup faster. Add a few dippers (graham cracker sticks or pretzels work well) right on top of each cup.

Make It Look Like Real Candy Corn

This recipe keeps things simple with a two-tone orange-and-white swirl. However, if you want the dip to look exactly like the candy, split the white mixture into two bowls before adding the orange food coloring. Leave one bowl white, tint one orange, and tint the last one yellow.

Layer them in a clear bowl from bottom to top — yellow, then orange, then white — instead of swirling, for a dip that mimics the classic three-color candy corn look.

Storage

Store covered tightly in the refrigerator up to 3–4 days. For the best texture and appearance, add the candy corn and sprinkles just before serving rather than storing them on top.

FAQ

Can I make this ahead of time?

Yes. You can prepare the dip up to a day ahead and keep it covered in the refrigerator. Wait to add the candy corn and sprinkles until just before serving.

What can I dip in it?

Vanilla wafers, graham crackers, pretzels, shortbread cookies, and apple slices are all great options for dipping.

Can I use regular food coloring instead of gel food coloring?

Yes. Regular liquid food coloring can be used, but you may need more to achieve a bright orange color. Add it gradually so you don’t add too much extra liquid.

Can I make this dip less sweet?

Yes. The powdered sugar can be reduced to suit your taste. Keep in mind that the pudding mix and whipped topping also add sweetness.

Can I freeze Candy Corn Dip?

I don’t recommend freezing it. The cream cheese and whipped topping can change texture when thawed, leaving the dip less smooth and creamy.

Candy Corn Dip

Estimated Cost: Cost: $8.26, $0.69 per Serving
This festive Candy Corn Dip has colorful layers of orange and white for a fun Halloween presentation. It’s creamy, sweet, and easy to serve with your favorite cookies, pretzels, or fruit.
Prep Time 10 minutes mins
Chill: 30 minutes mins
Total Time 40 minutes mins
Servings 12 (approximately ⅓ cup per serving) 
Cuisine American
Course Dessert
Calories 175

Ingredients

  • 1 3.4 oz box white chocolate instant pudding mix
  • 1 1/4 cups cold milk
  • 8 oz cream cheese softened
  • 1/2 cup powdered sugar use less for a less sweet dip
  • 1 tsp vanilla extract
  • 8 oz whipped topping thawed
  • Orange gel food coloring
  • Candy corn for garnish
  • Orange yellow, and white sprinkles, optional
Get Recipe Ingredients

See how we calculate recipe costs.

Instructions

  • Beat the cream cheese until smooth.
  • Add the powdered sugar and vanilla extract and beat until combined.
  • In a separate bowl, whisk the pudding mix and cold milk for about 2 minutes, until thickened.
  • Fold the pudding mixture into the cream cheese mixture until smooth.
  • Gently fold in the whipped topping until combined.
  • Reserve about ¼ cup of the mixture and set aside. Add orange gel food coloring to the remaining mixture until your desired color is reached.
  • Spread the orange dip into a serving bowl. Dollop the reserved white mixture on top and gently swirl with a toothpick to create a candy corn-inspired design.
  • Garnish with candy corn and sprinkles. Chill for 30 minutes before serving.
  • Serve with your favorite dippers and enjoy!

Recipe Notes

Best Dippers: Nilla Wafers, Golden Oreos, Graham crackers, Pretzels, Apple slices, Strawberries, Shortbread cookies
Storage: Store covered tightly in the refrigerator for up to 3–4 days.
